papers.title_in_file: Non-variational supervised quantum kernel methods: a review
papers.what_it_is: A review of non-variational supervised quantum kernel methods, their foundations, obstacles and empirical evidence.

assertions.value: The review states that it covers the foundations of non-variational supervised quantum kernel methods in classical kernel theory, fidelity and projected quantum kernels, advantage frameworks, exponential concentration and dequantisation.
quotes: In this review, we provide a thorough analysis of non-variational supervised QKMs, covering their foundations in classical kernel theory, constructions of fidelity and projected quantum kernels, and methods for their estimation in practice.
assertions.certainty_reason: The abstract states the review's own scope.

assertions.value: The review reports that benchmarking studies it cites reach a recurring conclusion: when classical baselines are carefully tuned, quantum kernels rarely demonstrate consistent or statistically significant performance improvements.
quotes: A recurring conclusion across these studies is that, when classical baselines are carefully tuned, quantum kernels rarely demonstrate consistent or statistically significant performance improvements.
In many cases, classical kernels with comparable effective complexity achieve similar or superior accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: A summary of other groups' benchmarks, not a result of the review itself.
assertions.reader_inference: Bears on any claim that a quantum kernel beats a tuned classical kernel.

assertions.value: The review states that dequantisation results constrain advantage claims for quantum kernel methods, showing efficient classical simulation under realistic data structures.
quotes: Additionally, dequantisation results further constrain such claims, demonstrating efficient classical simulations of QKMs under realistic data structures
assertions.certainty_reason: The review attributes this to cited work; it does not prove it here.

papers.title_in_file: Enabling Quantum Cybersecurity Analytics in Botnet Detection: Stable Architecture and Speed-up through Tree Algorithms
papers.what_it_is: An experimental study of hybrid quantum binary classifiers for DGA botnet detection, run on real quantum devices and simulators, with a Hoeffding-tree based classifier.

assertions.value: The authors report that their Quantum Hoeffding Tree Classifier, run on real-device-based simulation, reached an average accuracy of 91.2% and a final-round accuracy of 100% within a total computation time of 1,687 seconds, with the maximum sample size extended from 1,000 to 5,000.
quotes: We have extended the maximum sample size from 1,000 to 5,000 data samples in a quantum machine learning method, using real-device-based simulation through the Quantum Hoeffding Tree Classifier (QHTC) algorithm.
Our method achieves an average accuracy of 91.2% and a final-round accuracy of 100%, all within a total computation time of 1,687 seconds
assertions.certainty_reason: One study on one dataset, on real-device-based simulation rather than a real device.

assertions.value: The authors state that they beat the accuracy reported by Suryotrisongko and Musashi (76.8%) with an average accuracy of 91.2%.
quotes: Additionally, we beat their reported accuracy of 76.8% by an average accuracy of 91.2%
assertions.certainty_reason: A comparison across different setups (simulators against real-device-based simulation); the paper asserts it.
assertions.reader_inference: The two accuracies come from different platforms and sample sizes, so the comparison is not like for like.

assertions.value: The authors state that stability of computing and network elements is the primary limitation of cloud-based quantum computer delivery, and that they used a reduced sample size of 100 for real quantum devices.
quotes: We discovered that the stability of computing and network elements within the architecture is the primary limitation of cloud-based quantum computer delivery.
leading us to select a reduced sample size of 100 random fixed data points for real quantum devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limit in Section 4.1.

papers.title_in_file: Distributed Quantum Circuit Cutting for Hybrid Quantum-Classical High-Performance Computing
papers.what_it_is: A systems paper introducing Qdislib, a distributed circuit-cutting library for hybrid quantum-classical HPC, with scaling benchmarks.

assertions.value: The authors introduce Qdislib, a distributed library for quantum circuit cutting designed to integrate with hybrid quantum-classical HPC systems, and present a proof of concept of distributed execution across heterogeneous resources.
quotes: In this work, we introduce Qdislib, a distributed and flexible library for quantum circuit cutting, designed to seamlessly integrate with hybrid quantum-classical high-performance computing (HPC) systems.
We present a proof of concept demonstrating how Qdislib enables the distributed execution of quantum circuits across heterogeneous computing resources
assertions.certainty_reason: The abstract states the paper's own scope.

assertions.value: The authors report speedup for the 96-qubit HEA circuit with 4 cuts as nodes increase, with superlinear speedups in the first two transitions (1 to 2 and 2 to 4 nodes), and state that this shows circuit cutting with parallel execution has the potential to scale better when simulating large circuits.
quotes: Superlinear speedups are observed in the first two transitions: from 1 to 2 nodes and from 2 to 4 nodes.
Fig. 7. Speedup for the 96-qubit HEA circuit with 4 cuts.
This behavior confirms that circuit cutting combined with parallel execution has the potential to scale better, especially when simulating large quantum circuits.
assertions.certainty_reason: One system, one circuit family; the exact speedup figure sits next to a garbled multiplication sign in the text, so the value keeps to the quotes.

assertions.value: The authors state that wire cutting produces 8k subcircuit combinations and gate cutting produces 6k, where k is the number of cuts, and that the scaling stays exponential in the number of cuts.
quotes: with wire cutting producing 8k combinations and gate cutting producing 6k combinations, where k represents the number of cuts
Although the scaling remains exponential with the number of cuts
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the cost of cutting as its own stated limit (overview and Conclusion).

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Gradient Flow Algorithm for Symmetric Positive Definite Systems via Quantum Eigenvalue Transformation: Towards Quantum CAE
papers.what_it_is: A quantum algorithm for symmetric positive definite linear systems (QGFA), checked by simulation on small finite element problems.

assertions.value: The authors report that, on tensile and cantilever beam finite element simulations, QGFA reproduced the classical FEM solutions and achieved smaller relative errors than QMIA with fewer phase factors.
quotes: Through tensile and cantilever beam simulations, we confirmed that QGFA can accurately reproduce the classical FEM solutions.
Compared with QMIA, QGFA achieves smaller relative errors with fewer phase factors, demonstrating its potential as a numerically efficient alternative for SPD systems.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated results on small problems from one group.

assertions.value: The authors tested QGFA on a mesh of 9 quadrilateral elements for the tensile case and 3 quadrilateral elements for the cantilever beam case.
quotes: consisting of 16 nodes and 9 quadrilateral elements
Cantilever beam bending simulation with 3 quadrilateral elements solved by the FEM using QGFA
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own test setup.
assertions.reader_inference: Only very small problems were run, so scaling with the condition number of larger FEM matrices is not tested.

assertions.value: The authors state that QGFA converges best when an appropriate initial vector is provided, that accuracy and convergence depend on the condition number of the stiffness matrix, and that nonlinear and time-dependent problems are future work.
quotes: particularly when an appropriate initial vector u(0), i.e., a hot-start solution, is provided
the accuracy and convergence characteristics are found to depend on the condition number of the stiffness matrix K
Future work will focus on integrating QGFA with quantum iterative refinement techniques and exploring its applications to nonlinear and time-dependent problems
assertions.certainty_reason: The conclusion states these limits.

papers.title_in_file: Discovering Data Encoding Strategies for Quantum-Classical Neural Networks Using Monte Carlo Tree Search
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study that uses Monte Carlo tree search to find data encoding circuits for a quantum-classical convolutional network on two medical imaging datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that on two medical imaging datasets, automatically discovered encodings outperform commonly used encoding strategies and are competitive with classical baselines.
quotes: Our experiments on two medical imaging datasets demonstrate that automatically discovered encodings outperform commonly used encoding strategies and achieve competitive performance compared to classical baselines.
assertions.certainty_reason: Noiseless simulation on two small datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that feature map diversity (effective rank) correlates strongly with performance and can serve as an early rejection criterion, while entanglement capability and Fourier properties show weak correlation.
quotes: Our metric analysis reveals that feature map diversity correlates strongly with performance and can serve as an early rejection criterion to accelerate the search process, while entanglement capability and Fourier properties show weak correlation.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical correlation from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that all simulations are noiseless, experiments are limited to binary classification on small datasets, and their metrics do not certify a genuinely quantum computational advantage.
quotes: All simulations are performed in a noiseless environment, real quantum hardware may affect encoding performance.
Our experiments are limited to binary classification on small datasets with minimal classical components.
Importantly, our metrics measure representational richness and do not certify that the circuits provide a genuinely quantum computational advantage.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limits in Section VI.

papers.title_in_file: The Virtuous Cycle of Quantum-Classical Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, and the sections on variational circuits, quantum neural networks, generative models and quantum kernel methods; the reference list and remaining domain sections were not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: A perspective and review from Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI on how machine learning and quantum computing can benefit each other.

assertions.value: The authors state that they review the most salient opportunities for machine learning in quantum computing.
quotes: Here we review the most salient opportunities for machine learning in quantum computing, hoping to inspire a virtuous cycle through which both fields can mutually benefit.
assertions.certainty_reason: The abstract states the paper's scope.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum advantage is notoriously difficult to establish and that claims can be invalidated by later classical advances (dequantization).
quotes: Quantum advantage is notoriously difficult to establish, and such claims can be subsequently invalidated by further advances in classical methods, referred to as
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement about the field, backed by citations in the paper but not tested here.

assertions.value: The authors state, citing other work, that QCNN gradient variance decays no faster than polynomially but that QCNNs are also effectively classically simulable.
quotes: In QCNNs, the variance of the gradients decays no faster than polynomially
Yet, QCNNs are also effectively classically simulable
assertions.certainty_reason: The review attributes both results to cited papers.

assertions.value: The authors state that the theoretical efficiency of quantum kernel methods is often offset by a statistical sampling cost that scales polynomially with the desired accuracy.
quotes: is often offset by a statistical sampling cost that scales polynomially with the desired accuracy, representing a hurdle for real-world applications.
assertions.certainty_reason: An assertion by the authors in a perspective paper.

papers.title_in_file: A Comprehensive Analysis of Accuracy and Robustness in Quantum Neural Networks
papers.what_it_is: A simulation benchmark of QCNN, QRNN and QViT on MNIST and CIFAR-10 for accuracy, generalization and robustness to adversarial and quantum noise.

assertions.value: The authors report that on MNIST the three models reached 99.5% (QViT), 97.3% (QCNN) and 96.7% (QRNN), while on CIFAR-10 QViT reached the highest accuracy at 69.2% and QCNN the lowest at 55.5%.
quotes: With the MNIST dataset, a low-feature dataset, all three models achieved very high accuracy levels, namely 99.5% for QViT, 97.3% for QCNN, and 96.7% for QRNN.
The QViT model achieved the highest accuracy at 69.2%, while the QCNN model had the lowest at 55.5%.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation results from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that QViT is the most vulnerable of the three models to adversarial examples and that APGD was the most effective attack.
quotes: In contrast, QViT is highly sensitive to adversarial examples and the most vulnerable to attacks compared to the other two models.
Additionally, APGD proved to be the most effective attack method against QNN models
assertions.certainty_reason: One study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the transformer-based architecture kept high robustness against measurement noise, channel noise and finite-shot effects, while the other architectures declined markedly.
quotes: Conversely, in the presence of quantum noise, the transformer-based architecture proves its strength by maintaining high robustness against measurement noise, channel noise, and finite-shot effects
assertions.certainty_reason: One study, simulated noise models.

assertions.value: The authors state that the study is limited to binary classification for QRNN and QCNN, to image classification, and that the hyperparameter space was not thoroughly explored; tests on real quantum computers are future work.
quotes: The study is limited to binary classification for the QRNN and QCNN models, and the hyperparameter space has not been thoroughly investigated.
The benchmarking has been limited to image classification tasks
we will conduct further experiments to explore the impact of quantum noise on model accuracy on real quantum computers.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limits in Section 6.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Patches: Enhancing Robustness of Quantum Machine Learning Models
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study that uses random quantum circuits as pseudo-noise training data to reduce adversarial attack success rates of quantum classifiers.

assertions.value: The authors report that the RQC method reduced the adversarial attack success rate of the quantum classifier by 21.35% on CIFAR-10 and 15.55% on CINIC-10.
quotes: reducing the adversarial attack success rate (ASR) for the quantum classifier model by 21.35% on the CIFAR-10 dataset and 15.55% on the CINIC-10 dataset.
assertions.certainty_reason: One study, simulated attacks.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the low-feature MNIST dataset the RQC method did not make the model more robust, and the attack success rate rose from 22% to 25.38%.
quotes: it did not make the model more robust, as the ASR actually increased from 22% to 25.38%
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the method did not improve robustness for low-feature datasets such as MNIST, that the RQC pseudo-noise lowered model accuracy, and that the gain on QCNN was less pronounced than on the quantum classifier.
quotes: However, the proposed method still has limitations, as it did not improve robustness against adversarial attacks for low-feature datasets, such as MNIST.
Furthermore, the pseudo-noise generated by RQC also caused a decrease in the model's accuracy compared to when the RQC-enhanced method was not applied.
the improvement was not as pronounced as with the quantum classifier
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limits in Section VI.
